scope: Canonical solution architecture for the approved Windows-only Sandwich Download Manager v0.1. Implementation and independent verification remain downstream responsibilities.

architectureDecisions.decision: Use one Rust workspace with a UI-independent download-engine library consumed by a Tauri Windows application.
architectureDecisions.rationale: This implements DEC-20260803-003, prevents business-rule drift, and keeps the native-webview shell thin.
constraints: Tauri commands translate inputs and outputs but do not implement domain policy

architectureDecisions.decision: The engine owns a durable download aggregate and per-segment checkpoints; metadata updates are atomic and final output is published only after byte-complete assembly succeeds.
architectureDecisions.rationale: Pause, restart, and network recovery require one authoritative lifecycle and persistence contract.
invariants: completed is terminal and is recorded only after finalization succeeds
cancelled is terminal and cannot resume
partial and metadata files are never exposed as completed output
persisted segment offsets never exceed their inclusive byte ranges
resume accepts only valid HTTP 206 responses with matching Content-Range; otherwise the engine safely restarts or uses the single-stream fallback
every resolved output path remains beneath the selected destination

architectureDecisions.decision: Probe Range support before segmentation; use bounded parallel byte ranges only when the server proves compliant, and restart as a single stream when it ignores Range.
architectureDecisions.rationale: Range behavior varies by server and an invalid partial response must never be assembled as if it were a segment.

architectureDecisions.decision: Manual entry and clipboard detection call the same URL-intake service; clipboard input creates an ephemeral offer and never queues or starts a transfer without confirmation.
architectureDecisions.rationale: One validation path avoids inconsistent behavior and prevents unrelated clipboard content from being persisted.

architectureDecisions.decision: Filename derivation, Windows-name sanitization, type organization, collision resolution, and final path containment are engine services; open and reveal are fallible Windows adapter actions invoked only for completed files.
architectureDecisions.rationale: Untrusted HTTP metadata and OS shell invocation are trust boundaries and must not be reimplemented in UI code.

adapterContracts.name: submit_url
adapterContracts.rule: Calls the shared intake and queue service.

adapterContracts.name: list_downloads
adapterContracts.rule: Snapshots include status, completed_bytes, total_bytes, bytes_per_second, eta_seconds, and recoverable error details.

adapterContracts.name: clipboard_candidate
adapterContracts.rule: Non-URLs are discarded; offers are not persisted and do not start downloads.

adapterContracts.name: open_completed_file|reveal_completed_file
adapterContracts.rule: The engine resolves the stored completed path; the Windows adapter performs the shell action without interpolated shell commands.

transitions.guard: checkpoint current offsets before acknowledging pause

transitions.action: discard incompatible segment bodies and restart one bounded single stream

lifecycle.restartRecovery: On startup, active records become recoverably_interrupted after manifests and partial files are validated; queued and paused states remain stable; terminal states never restart automatically.

capabilityOwnership.capability: segmented URL download and Range fallback
pause, resume, cancel, restart and network recovery
destination, organization, collision, safe filename and file actions
capabilityOwnership.uiOrAdapterRole: folder selection and Windows shell execution only

systemImpacts.impact: URLs, redirects, Content-Disposition, paths, and shell actions are untrusted; scheme allowlisting, redirect policy, path containment, reserved-name handling, and argument-safe OS APIs are required.
Clipboard text is inspected in memory only; unrelated or dismissed content is not persisted or logged.
Atomic versioned manifests and partial files are local to the application data and selected destination boundaries; no database or migration is required for v0.1.
Checkpoint-before-acknowledgement and restart validation prevent silent corruption across pause, network loss, and process restart.
Segment count, concurrent downloads, and progress-event frequency are explicitly bounded; blocking filesystem work cannot run on the UI thread.
Queue changes need semantic live status, discernible labels, visible focus, and keyboard-operable controls verified in the Windows runtime.
Windows compilation requires Rust, Node tooling, Microsoft C++ build tools, and WebView2; production deployment and signing are outside this request.
GPL-3.0 text is required at the repository root, but that path is outside this workstream's allowed write boundary.

downstreamEvidenceBoundary: Transfer behavior requires controlled HTTP integration tests with byte/hash comparison.
User-visible behavior requires a real Tauri/WebView DOM or equivalent Windows runtime test, including keyboard and assistive-technology checks.
Only ENG-15 may issue the independent engineering verification disposition.
implementationNotes: Downstream crates and adapters must consume the shared engine rather than duplicate state, URL, filename, collision, progress, or recovery rules.
Use typed commands, snapshots, and errors across the Tauri boundary; do not expose filesystem paths supplied directly by the webview to open/reveal APIs.
No source implementation existed when this baseline was recorded, so this artifact makes no buildability or runtime-behavior claim.
knownRisks: The authoritative write boundary excludes root Cargo.toml and LICENSE even though approved acceptance criteria require them.
Servers may misreport length, validators, or Range behavior; downstream tests must cover malformed and changing responses.
Atomic rename, antivirus locks, disk exhaustion, Windows reserved names, long paths, and unavailable destinations need filesystem integration coverage.
Speed and ETA require smoothing and an explicit unknown state to avoid misleading users early in a transfer.
Tauri runtime accessibility and responsiveness remain unverified until a real Windows build exists.
Independent verification remains pending for ENG-15.
